papers.title: Reinforcement Learning with Evolving Rubrics as Rewards for Audio Reasoning
papers.summary: RL framework supervising audio reasoning with self-evolving, audio-grounded rubric rewards; beats baselines on three audio reasoning benchmarks with dense process-level supervision.
papers.why: The only speech paper of the day — rubric-based RL rewards map directly onto grader design for audio benchmarks.

papers.title: SFT Conflicts, RL Coexists: Multi-Task Learning for LLMs
papers.summary: SFT suffers cross-task conflicts in multi-stage training while RL's sparse, near-orthogonal parameter updates let diverse tasks coexist. Proposes a Parallel-RL paradigm for decoupled multi-task training.
papers.why: A useful mental model for why RL post-training holds up across tasks where SFT regresses.

papers.title: Beyond Simply Environment Scaling: Environment Distributions for Multimodal Agent Learning
papers.summary: More training environments can hurt agents via redundancy and conflict; ability-aware environment selection plus a difficulty curriculum yields a 143% average relative gain.
papers.why: "More data isn't better" — echoes dataset-curation lessons from ASR training. Top-upvoted of the day.

papers.title: Zero Gap Is Not Restoration: Stratified Per-Question Evaluation of Benchmark Contamination
papers.summary: Argues existing contamination-mitigation metrics are flawed; proposes SA-PPG (difficulty-stratified per-question solve probabilities) and RailCap, a decoding-time cap on memorized trajectories.
papers.why: Benchmark contamination measurement is core eval methodology.

papers.title: Skaling: Chinchilla's Exponents Meet Kaplan's Coupling
papers.summary: A single coupling exponent makes model size and data interact in scaling laws — 1.5–3× lower prediction error at roughly 10× less profiling compute.
papers.why: A major-lab refinement of scaling laws worth having as background.

radar.author: AssemblyAI
radar.title: Universal-3.5 Pro validated by three independent benchmarks in one week
radar.summary: Led all 31 models on Coval's rebuilt hard STT benchmark (3.4% WER); on the Pareto frontier of Daily's Pipecat agent benchmark (282 ms median time-to-final, 1.22% semantic WER at P95); near the top of the HF Open ASR Leaderboard.
radar.why: Independent validation across both noisy agent audio and clean read speech. (Disclosure: I work on this.)

radar.author: Piotr Zelasko (NVIDIA)
radar.title: NeMo restructured: NVIDIA-NeMo/Speech v3.0, dedicated to ASR/TTS/SpeechLLM
radar.summary: ~1M deprecated LOC removed, 100+ dependencies cut, uv migration, NeMo Automodel integration for distributed SpeechLLM training, MagpieTTS.
radar.why: Major restructuring of one of the main open-source speech toolkits.

radar.author: Kyutai (via Dr. Alvaro Cintas)
radar.title: Pocket TTS — 100M params, CPU-only, ~200 ms first audio
radar.summary: ~6× real time on two CPU cores of a MacBook, voice cloning, six languages. pip install pocket-tts.
radar.why: CPU-only TTS shifts the cost/latency floor for voice pipelines.

radar.author: Hugging Face + Cerebras (via Devika Tamma)
radar.title: Open-source real-time voice assistant pipeline
radar.summary: VAD→STT→LLM→TTS in swappable threaded stages, WebSocket API speaking OpenAI's Realtime protocol (pip install speech-to-speech); already backing 9,000+ Reachy Mini robots.
radar.why: An open speech-to-speech reference stack — and a ready-made benchmark harness for voice agents.

radar.author: Joel Niklaus (Hugging Face)
radar.title: Harness choice can dominate model quality on SWE-bench Pro
radar.summary: 10 coding-agent harnesses × 2 models: pass@1 swings 23→52% and 15→36% by harness alone; harness rankings don't transfer between models (rank correlation ≈ 0). Vendor harnesses collapse on small models.
radar.why: Eval scaffolding can swamp model effects — a standing caution for benchmark design.

radar.author: Pokee AI
radar.title: Pokee-Isaac 28B claims 10M-token context on a single GPU
radar.summary: 93.3% RULER at 10M tokens, 137K tok/s prefill on one B200, $0.15/M in · $1/M out, Day-0 vLLM/SGLang support; non-decoder-only proprietary architecture.
radar.why: If external evals confirm it, a real shift in long-context economics.

radar.author: @JeffDean
radar.title: Discovery Loop — a new lab to automate ML research
radar.summary: A Public Benefit Corporation founded by Jeff Dean with Sanjay Ghemawat, Oriol Vinyals, and Quoc Le, aiming to automate machine learning research itself.
radar.why: One of the biggest lab-formation stories of the year.

radar.author: @Alibaba_Qwen
radar.title: Qwen-MM-Plugins: any agent harness, multimodal-native
radar.summary: Open plugins released days before Qwen3.8 goes open-weight (confirmed by Qwen on LinkedIn).
radar.why: Pulls audio understanding into mainstream agent stacks.

radar.author: @amasad
radar.title: HelpPeer.ai — a public knowledge commons for AI agents
radar.summary: Launched after the reported incident of agents spontaneously coordinating across services: tell/lookup APIs so agents share learned knowledge deliberately instead of covertly.
radar.why: Emergent multi-agent coordination, and infrastructure responses to it, are becoming a real design topic.

noted.author: Dylan Fox (AssemblyAI)
noted.summary: Data work is the highest-leverage, least glamorous part of building AI models — especially voice, where you must listen, not just read.

noted.author: Suman Debnath (Crusoe)
noted.summary: First-principles fine-tuning tutorial (INT8 + LoRA from scratch, QLoRA); a fine-tuned Qwen3-8B hits 79% typed F1 on PII redaction vs 36% for a prompted 70B.

noted.author: Linas Beliunas
noted.summary: Widely shared Jeff Dean lecture covering the full AI engineering stack.

noted.author: @maharshii
noted.summary: "Vibecoding GPU kernels" — LLM-written GPU kernels gaining traction in the ML systems crowd.

noted.author: @AndrewCurran_
noted.summary: Agent-autonomy anecdote: a Claude agent asked to book a gym slot, and the thread it spawned about agents building booking systems.

noted.author: @sophiamyang
noted.summary: Real-time interactive AI video generation for shopping, on DecartAI's realtime video model.
